grh_2546acbd1aad78eae0fa.title: Revolt
paragraphs: Nineteen-year-old Bill and Helen arrive in Rivers End posing as brother and sister after running away from Minneapolis. Resentful of what he calls a system that keeps young people powerless, Bill plans to rob Dr. Christian's safe and pressures Helen to learn the combination, eventually threatening the doctor with a gun. Dr. Christian has already recognized their lies, found the police bulletin and quietly removed the cartridges from Bill's weapon. Confronted with how completely his rebellion has turned into crime, Bill abandons the robbery and decides to return voluntarily, face the consequences and then work honestly toward a future. Helen's mother is coming to take her home, and the two young people leave their marriage plans for a more responsible time.

The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_25f963e6556e2dad7b64.title: Official Killer
paragraphs: Samuel Jones has spent years as the state’s official hangman, taking pride in carrying out hundreds of executions. After hanging a young prisoner, he is confronted by the man’s mother and learns that the condemned youth was his own son. The shock unleashes a nightmare procession of the relatives of people he has executed, all seeming to pursue him through the streets, until the terrified hangman barricades himself indoors and kills himself before the imagined mob can reach him.

grh_25e0bf654b9958b66c91.title: Your School Your Children
paragraphs: A dramatization of Marie Syrkin's Your School, Your Children argues that public schools must directly confront racial, religious and political prejudice rather than avoiding controversial subjects. Classroom and faculty scenes show antisemitism, anti-Black bias and administrative reluctance to challenge intolerance, while Syrkin worries that students can carry those attitudes into adult life. The broadcast points to the Springfield Plan as a working model that teaches democratic self-government, evidence-based judgment and respect for every individual as part of the regular curriculum.
